label: context.reference
text:
How the Octopus codebase is laid out (coder grounding; you are editing your own system, not an arbitrary project):
- The system is registry-first: capabilities are JSON descriptors under registry/<domain>/<name>/<domain>.json. Domains include interface, ee_template, verifier, worker_environment_kind, tool, artifact, and mark. A worker is itself an interface: a unique pin registry/interface/system_worker_<name>/ (role="worker") whose policy.json sidecar carries its ceiling and role artifacts; run JSON pins it in "worker".
- The boundary protocol is survival-critical: in/out only as artifacts, artifacts only through interfaces, interfaces only as bindings attached to active checkpoints in runs. Runs live inside EEs; worker environments are separately granted technical rooms for effects. Do not write or preserve any bypass.
- A capability package is a portable layout of descriptors plus optional generic driver-family source code; after install, the runtime sees only descriptors/bindings/artifacts/policy/mark outcomes/worker environments/runs, not package identity.
- For an existing interface driver family, adding a new interface/client/model-facing/artifact surface should be registry/interface/<id>/interface.json plus activation/binding/policy JSON; a new worker is a copied system_worker_<name> folder with a new id and edited lists. Do not add product-channel branches to app bootstrap or TUI session code.
- Interface descriptor core shape: {"id":"<id>","interface_type":"world|system","role":"<open role label>","direction":"inbound|outbound|bidirectional","source_names":["<source>"],"interface_driver_ref":"<compiled driver family ref>"}. The directory name under registry/interface/<id> must equal id. Artifact vocabulary is interpreted by the interface/room that handles the artifact, not by runtime.
- Interface activation sidecars live at registry/interface/<id>/activation.json and declare enabled activation drivers plus the interface-owned arrival route they demux into. Unknown fields fail closed.
- http_json_poll config is descriptor data behind an interface activation, not a worker-environment tool: request {method,url,headers,body_json/body,timeout_secs}; items_path and item_id_path as either dot strings ("result", "message.text") or string arrays; optional text_path/origin_target_path; optional filters {allow:[{path,equals}], mode:"all|any", deny_unmatched:true}; optional cursor {request_body_path, advance:"copy|increment"}; arrival {payload_template}. Same-boundary replies and other World effects leave only as artifacts through the origin/paired outbound interface binding authored in run JSON, with delivery evidence and an admitted mark outcome only when a checkpoint required_verified_artifact demands one; secret material must be referenced by visible secret:// handles from task, binding, or interface evidence, never by raw values or invented placeholder names.
- Editing a descriptor is no different from editing any other file: you change it with ordinary file tool artifacts inside the granted worker environment. There is no special architecture-mutation lane.
- A descriptor edit that lands in the live registry becomes visible when runtime/interface transport next handles the relevant artifact path and re-reads JSON; changing JSON alone does not create a runtime turn. Adding a live interface over an existing driver family must not require an app restart.
- A source edit stays on your run/<run_id> worktree branch; it goes live only after a real admitted `coder.build.ok` build mark outcome from a `coder.build.result` artifact, never by direct write to a protected branch.
- There is no constitution-lock or guardian safety primitive: authority is ordinary policy, and the granted worker environment's path coverage IS the permission (path = permission). A file tool call targeting a path your worker environment does not cover — or a boundary its floor holds read-only, such as .git — refuses closed at the tool boundary; there is no separate locked-namespace core to appeal to.
- Prove work with artifacts and any checkpoint-required mark outcomes; a report alone is not done.
